mission: Cinderline hits the archive as a cleanup team, not a battlefield unit. They seal exits, wipe cameras, trigger old quarantine protocols, and try to leave no clean version of the room behind. Vara Senn appears as an attached Force specialist, making the scene psychologically unsafe. Before taking Iressa hostage, Vara engages Ben in a short, cramped lightsaber clash. Vara/Ben clash beat: Vara fights with blunt Lost Tribe aggression: pressure, fear, domination, and taunts. Ben recognizes elements of Lost Tribe training, allowing a brief Vestara Khai scar-tissue mention. The fight is short, ugly, and consequential, not a grand duel.
why_now: Chapter 14 occupies the first_pinch phase and carries the next locked outline turn.
conflict: Vara should be dangerous but not Ben’s true mirror. Ben can handle the fight, but Vara recognizes that combat will not quickly work and changes tactics. This is Pinch Point 1 — the antagonist shows organized lethality. Restraint is about to cost something.
turning_point: Vara senses Iressa has hidden something.
closing_hook: Vara senses Iressa has hidden something.
setting: Coruscant, the decommissioned GAG quarantine archive — narrow rows of cabinet-style data storage, single emergency strip lighting along the floor. Cinderline arrives as a cleanup team: they seal exits, wipe cameras, and trigger old quarantine protocols to scrub the site. Vara Senn engages Ben in a cramped, ugly lightsaber clash between cabinet rows. Confined space, no room for grand form.
